pros: Shop Pay checkout finishes returning shoppers in a couple of taps
App store covers subscriptions, returns and loyalty without custom code
Theme editor lets non-developers rearrange sections and app blocks
Sidekick answers questions grounded in your own store data
Markets handles multi-currency pricing, duties and localised domains
cons: Paid apps and gateway fees push real cost well above plan price
Standard catalogue model strains under complex configurations and B2B pricing
Native recommendations, bundles and cart upsells need third-party apps
Built-in inventory reports cannot forecast demand or raise purchase orders
verdict_line: Pick Shopify if you want a hosted store with a checkout you never maintain and an app for every specialist function.

pros: Rules engine filters recommendations by tag, price band, stock or metafield
Smart Cart adds shipping progress bars and tiered gifts without theme code
Built-in A/B testing reports revenue per widget variant
Recharge integration keeps recommendations aware of subscription status
Post-purchase offers appear between checkout and the thank-you page
cons: Pricing scales with order volume, costly for high-volume thin-margin stores
Injected JavaScript can slow storefronts already running several apps
Recommendations stay generic until months of order history accumulate
Only works on Shopify and Shopify Plus stores
verdict_line: Pick Rebuy if you run a Shopify store with enough order history to feed personalised upsells and a cart worth optimising.

pros: Bulk competitor URL upload via spreadsheet gets data within a day
Alerts fire when a rival changes price, undercuts you or sells out
Repricing rules respect minimum margin bounds per brand or category
Competitor stock tracking lets you hold price when rivals sell out
Repriced values push to Shopify, Magento or WooCommerce automatically
cons: Product matching is manual and breaks when competitors change URLs
Rules are logic-based, no demand elasticity or profit optimisation
Competitor sites with strong bot protection leave gaps in data
Nothing for the storefront side such as bundling or recommendations
verdict_line: Pick Prisync if you compete on price across a mid-sized catalogue and need daily competitor data without building scrapers.

pros: Replenishment report shows order quantity and date per variant
Stockout periods are excluded rather than counted as zero demand
Draft purchase orders group by supplier with MOQ and case packs applied
Bundles forecast component demand from the kits that consume them
Overstock reports quantify cash tied up in slow movers
cons: Forecasts are weak for new launches, promotions and short-lifecycle ranges
Volume-based pricing climbs as the store grows
Dense settings mean accurate setup takes days, mostly on your team
Planning only, no warehouse management, picking or order routing
verdict_line: Pick Inventory Planner if you reorder a stable multichannel catalogue and want purchase orders built from forecasts, not spreadsheets.
